methods.label: Scale area and weight
methods.explanation:
The two equilateral triangles are similar, with length scale factor \(5/3\). Both the base and its corresponding height scale by this factor, so their areas have ratio
\[
\frac{\text{second area}}{\text{first area}}
=\left(\frac53\right)^2=\frac{25}{9}.
\]
Equal density and thickness make the weight per square inch the same for both pieces. Consequently, the second piece weighs
\[
12\cdot\frac{25}{9}=\frac{100}{3}
=33\frac13\text{ ounces}.
\]
The closest listed weight is \(33.3\) ounces, choice D.
